[[File:Jessica Tui Dempsey (born 1978) in the video 'POWEHI - Hawai'i and the Event Horizon Telescope'.png|thumb|Dempsey in the video ''POWEHI - Hawai'i and the Event Horizon Telescope'' (2019)]]
'''Jessica Tui Dempsey''' (born 1978) is an Australian [[radio astronomy|radio astronomer]] and the incoming director-general of the [[Square Kilometre Array]] Observatory. Her research focuses on the molecular composition of the [[Milky Way]]; as part of the [[Event Horizon Telescope]] team she also participated in creating the first images of [[supermassive black hole]]s.{{r|ska}} She has been described as "a strong advocate for greater diversity, equality and opportunity in astronomy".{{r|run}}

After growing up on a livestock farm in the outback,{{r|nwo}} secondary education at [[Mary MacKillop College, Kensington]] from 1991 to 1995, and participation at the [[National Youth Science Forum]],{{r|mmc}} Dempsey studied both astrophysics and theatre and film science as an undergraduate at the [[University of New South Wales]] (UNSW),{{r|ska}} and in the late 1990s she worked as an actress.{{r|nwo}} In 2000 she began working on the [[Arcminute Cosmology Bolometer Array Receiver]] at the [[South Pole]],{{r|ska}} for her master's thesis,{{r|nwo}} one of the first two Australian women to work as scientists at the pole, and in 2005 the first to spend the winter there.{{r|ska}} She completed a Ph.D. through UNSW in 2005, with the dissertation ''The view from the ice at the bottom of the world: Optical astronomy from Antarctica'' supervised by John W. V. Storey.{{r|ag}}

She moved to the [[James Clerk Maxwell Telescope]] in Hawaii in 2007, was named as an astronomer and operations manager in 2012, and became deputy director of the telescope in 2016.{{r|ska|jcmt}} She was named as director of [[ASTRON]], the Netherlands Institute for Radio Astronomy, for a term beginning in 2022.{{r|ska|astron}} She added an affiliation as Professor by special appointment for Ethics in Astronomy at [[Radboud University Nijmegen]] in 2023.{{r|run}} In 2025 she was announced as the next director of the Square Kilometre Array Observatory, for a five-year term beginning in 2026.{{r|ska}}
